- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. <function call omitted for brevity>

user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. - pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. ## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)

You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

content.text:
Based on each ticket's **Definition of Done**:

## SFCC-122 — MRT API Capabilities
**Deliverable:** A documented inventory of relevant SFCC MRT APIs, shared with the squad — enough to unblock BM configuration and front-end development in lower environments while MuleSoft isn't ready.

Concretely, that doc should cover (per the Tasks section):
1. Endpoint structure, payload format, auth, and data available for each relevant MRT API
2. Which MRT APIs can stand in for product/category/pricing data in lower environments
3. Gaps/limitations that will still need MuleSoft once it's ready
4. Which MRT APIs are permanent architecture vs. temporary workarounds

## SFCC-123 — Contentful Integration TSD
**Deliverable:** A technical design document covering the Contentful integration architecture, content model requirements, locale setup, and SFCC-side build scope — written as a briefing artefact for the incoming Contentful squad.

Concretely, that doc should cover:
1. The Contentful → MRT → SFCC integration pattern and data flow
2. Required content types for Sprint 1 & 2 (page layouts, content slots, editorial components)
3. What SFCC needs to consume from Contentful — APIs, content model fields, rendering logic
4. Locale configuration requirements aligned to the 8 storefronts
5. The handoff boundary — what Accenture builds vs. what the Contentful squad owns
6. Any blockers/dependencies to resolve before that squad onboards

So: **two documents**, one MRT API inventory and one Contentful TSD — both ultimately living in `.docs/` (integration docs) once produced, per this project's convention of `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` for how integrations work technically.

**Architecture:** Single Contentful space with one environment per delivery tier.

Environment Topology
--------------------

Six-tier delivery pipeline. Contentful environment IDs map directly to MRT push targets.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | MRT URL |

| 1 & 2 | DEV | `dev` | `npm run push:dev` | zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

| 6 | UAT | `uat` | `npm run push:uat` | zimmermann-uat.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 7 | PRODUCTION | `master` (via `production` alias) | `npm run push:prod` | zimmermann-production.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

Promotion order: **dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master**

Alias Strategy & Release Workflow
---------------------------------

Two aliases are maintained and always kept in sync:

* `production` — what MRT production tier uses (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`). Flipping this is the zero-downtime release mechanism.
* `master` — Contentful’s built-in alias, kept in sync with `production`.

### Release workflow

1. Create a release environment in the Contentful web UI: clone from the current `production` target, name it `release-YYYY-MM`.
2. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM`
3. Test against the release environment directly (bypasses the alias).
4. Promote: `npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM` (flips both aliases atomically).
5. Retain the previous environment for 14 days as a rollback target, then delete.

The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan. The `master` alias is always available as the built-in fallback.

API Keys & Tokens
-----------------

| Variable | Scope | Local .env | GitHub Actions | MRT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` | Space (shared) | ✓ | Variable | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | Per tier | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Per env, read-only | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |

| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Per user (personal) | ✓ | Secret (CI service account) | **Never** |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Per env | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |

### CI service account CMA token

Create a dedicated Contentful user (e.g. `contentful-ci@zimmermann.com`), invite as Space Administrator,
log in as that user and generate a Personal Access Token under Account Settings → CMA Tokens.
Store as the `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret.

### Per-developer setup

Each developer generates their own CMA token: **Contentful → top-right avatar → Account Settings → CMA Tokens → Create personal access token**.
Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Delivery and preview tokens are space-level — run `npm run config:contentful` to populate them automatically.

Locale Configuration
--------------------

Nine locales matching SFCC `config/sites.js` exactly. No runtime mapping required.

| Locale Code | Name | Storefront(s) | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `en` | English (AU) | ZimmermannAU | Default |
| `en-US` | English (US) | ZimmermannUS | en |
| `en-GB` | English (UK / EU) | ZimmermannUK, ZimmermannEUen | en |
| `fr` | French | ZimmermannEUfr | en |

| `en-HK` | English (HK) | ZimmermannHK | en |
| `en-AE` | English (ME) | ZimmermannME | en |

Locales are created in the `master` environment during bootstrap; cloned environments inherit them automatically. All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`.

Content Type Management
-----------------------

|  | Editorial content types | Studio Experiences definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` |
| **Deploy** | `npm run sync:contentful` or migration | Imported at runtime — no push step |

// Use the contentful-management plain client

Drift Detection & Promotion Rules
---------------------------------

* **Contentful roles:** Assign a “Content Editor” role on `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, and `master` that can CRUD entries/assets but cannot edit content types. Only the CI service account can modify content types in those environments.
* **Migration runner** calls `detectDrift` automatically before applying. Use `--force` to bypass.

bashwide4000npm run detect:drift -- --source dev --target sit

    "content": {
      "value": "1-overview1. Overview
---------------------

Product data in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is managed through a **master catalogue** (`zimmermann-catalog`) with per-site **storefront catalogues** for navigation and category assignment. Product content (rich text, editorial imagery) is managed in **Contentful CMS**.

AP21 is the system of record for all product data. Product data flows from AP21 into SFCC via **MuleSoft** — there is no direct AP21 → SFCC integration. MuleSoft acts as the integration layer, transforming and routing product data into SFCC catalogue XML imports.

---

2-product-data-architecture2. Product Data Architecture
-------------------------------------------------------

DefaultnoneAP21 (ERP — system of record for products)
│
└──► MuleSoft (integration layer — transform + route)
│
└──► zimmermann-catalog (SFCC master catalogue)
│ products + variants + attributes
│
├──► zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog (AU nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-uk-storefront-catalog (UK nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-us-storefront-catalog (US domestic nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-us-intl-storefront-catalog (US International / Global-e nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-eu-storefront-catalog (EU nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-eu-intl-storefront-catalog (EU International / Global-e nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-hk-storefront-catalog (HK nav categories)
└──► zimmermann-me-storefront-catalog (ME nav categories)
Contentful CMS
│
└──► PWA Kit (editorial content: banners, editorial copy, lookbook)
via Contentful Delivery API

---

3-master-catalogue-structure3. Master Catalogue Structure
---------------------------------------------------------

**Catalogue ID:**`zimmermann-catalog`

### 31-category-hierarchy-all-storefront-catalogues3.1 Category Hierarchy (all storefront catalogues)

| Position | Category ID | Display Name | Sub-categories |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `new-arrivals` | New | — |
| 2 | `clothing` | Clothing | dresses, tops, bottoms, knitwear, jackets, swimwear |
| 3 | `accessories` | Accessories | bags, shoes, jewellery |
| 4 | `collections` | Collections | resort |
| 5 | `z-immerse` | Z.Immerse | — |
| 6 | `sale` | Sale | — |

**Magento-sourced category hierarchy** (used during Magento migration — see Section 11):

Defaultnoneroot
└── {prodline} (L1 — e.g. "collection")
└── {prodline}-{prodsub} (L2 — product assignment target, e.g. "collection-tops-blouse")

`categoryap21` is an internal AP21 ERP code — stored as a hidden custom attribute (`ap21Category`) on the product, not used for storefront navigation.

### 32-product-model3.2 Product Model

SFCC product types in use:

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Master product | Top-level product identified by `stylecode` — holds variation attributes (colour, size), images, descriptions |
| Variant product | Individual purchasable SKU — `stylecode` + `colourcode` + `sizecode` |
| Color group (Magento) | Style + colour SKU in Magento (`visibility = Catalog, Search`) — maps to master product body |

**Product ID conventions:**

| SFCC Role | ID Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Master | `stylecode` | `4673TS251` |
| Variant | `stylecode` + `colourcode` + `sizecode` | `4673TS251GVSCP0P` |

---

4-catalogue-import-process4. Catalogue Import Process
-----------------------------------------------------

### 41-initial-load-sample-data4.1 Initial Load (Sample Data)

A filtered sample catalogue (`data/sample/catalogs/zimmermann-catalog/`) is used for development and staging bootstrapping.

**Import command:**

Defaultbashnpm run data:import:sample

### 42-ongoing-product-feed4.2 Ongoing Product Feed

| Step | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Source | AP21 (ERP) — system of record for all product master data |
| Integration layer | MuleSoft — receives product events from AP21, transforms to SFCC Catalog XML, and delivers to SFCC |
| Format | SFCC Catalog XML (catalog.xsd compliant) |
| Target | `zimmermann-catalog` (master) + per-site storefront catalogues |
| Trigger | MuleSoft event-driven (AP21 product create / update) or scheduled batch — to be confirmed with MuleSoft team |
| Import method | MuleSoft → SFCC OCAPI Data API (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or SFCC SFTP + import job |

### 43-product-imagery4.3 Product Imagery

Product images are loaded directly into SFCC — there is no Cloudinary or external DAM involved. Images are stored in the SFCC static content library and referenced from product records by path.

| Aspect | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Storage | SFCC static content library (loaded directly) |
| Source | AP21 / DAM — images are uploaded directly to SFCC; no Cloudinary or external DAM in the pipeline |
| Image types | Large, medium, small/thumbnail, hi-res model shot, swatch/styling shot |
| Migration reference | Magento image paths used as source reference during initial load only |

---

5-storefront-catalogue-assignment5. Storefront Catalogue Assignment
-------------------------------------------------------------------

Each site's storefront catalogue is set in `preferences.xml` via `SiteCatalog`:

| Site | Storefront Catalogue |
| --- | --- |
| ZimmermannAU | `zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannUK | `zimmermann-uk-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannUS | `zimmermann-us-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannUSIntl | `zimmermann-us-intl-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannEU | `zimmermann-eu-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannEUIntl | `zimmermann-eu-intl-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannHK | `zimmermann-hk-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannME | `zimmermann-me-storefront-catalog` |

The master catalogue assignment (linking storefront categories to master products) is managed in SFCC Business Manager — it cannot be set via XML import.

---

6-contentful-cms-integration6. Contentful CMS Integration
---------------------------------------------------------

| Aspect | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Editorial content: hero banners, collection pages, lookbook, rich PDP copy |
| Rendering | PWA Kit fetches content at runtime via Contentful Delivery API |
| Scope | Non-product content; all product data remains in SFCC catalogue sourced from AP21 via MuleSoft |

---

7-multilocale-product-content7. Multi-Locale Product Content
------------------------------------------------------------

| Site | Locales | Language Tags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ZimmermannAU | en | `x-default`, `en` |
| ZimmermannUK | en, en\_GB | `x-default`, `en`, `en-GB` |
| ZimmermannUS | en, en\_US | `x-default`, `en`, `en-US` |
| ZimmermannUSIntl | en, en\_US | `x-default`, `en`, `en-US` |
| ZimmermannEU | en, en\_GB, fr, it, es | `x-default`, `en`, `fr`, `it`, `es` |
| ZimmermannEUIntl | en, en\_CH | `x-default`, `en`, `en-CH` |
| ZimmermannHK | en, en\_HK | `x-default`, `en`, `en-HK` |
| ZimmermannME | en, en\_AE | `x-default`, `en`, `en-AE` |

Product XML attributes use `xml:lang` for each locale. The `x-default` value is always English.

---

8-product-display-page-pdp--mulesoft-touchpoints8. Product Display Page (PDP) — MuleSoft Touchpoints
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

MuleSoft is the integration layer for the product import pipeline (see Section 4.2). In addition, the PDP has two further MuleSoft-dependent runtime features:

| Feature | API | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find In Store / Boutique Stock | `product-availibility-prc-api` | Real-time store stock availability shown on PDP |
| Real-time DC stock check | [TBC] | Online availability from NewStore fulfilment groups |

---

9-key-design-decisions9. Key Design Decisions
---------------------------------------------

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product source of truth | AP21 | AP21 is the ERP and master for all product data |
| Product integration layer | MuleSoft | Consistent with Zimmermann integration platform; MuleSoft handles AP21 event consumption, transformation, and SFCC delivery |

content.text:
I've searched the SFCC Confluence space and pulled the full content of the most relevant pages. Here's the audit for both spikes.

## SFCC-122 — MRT API Capabilities

**No dedicated page exists yet** documenting MRT API capabilities — confirmed by the [Dependencies](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/310050860) page, which tracks "**T2 — SFCC MRT API Capabilities**" as a Squad A / Sprint 1 dependency with **blank SME Owner, Status, and Notes**. This spike is the thing that's supposed to fill that row in — it's a real gap, not duplicated work.

Supporting context that exists:
- **[TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208)** §4.2/§10 — names the target MRT-native surface: MuleSoft is expected to deliver via SFCC's **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or SFTP+import job — but this is listed as **Open Item #1, unconfirmed**. Also flags PDP's two MuleSoft-dependent runtime features (`product-availability-prc-api`, and a TBC real-time DC stock API) as things that don't exist yet.
- **[Product Integration Register](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/257163278)** (INT-013, INT-033) — confirms product/price data via MuleSoft is "Under Review," P0, with open attribute-mapping questions — this is the "why" behind the spike (Mani's note that BM config is in place but data is missing).
- **[MuleSoft Integration — Open Questions for SFCC/PWA Design](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/320602113)** — a large, mostly-❓-unanswered questionnaire for the MuleSoft team covering product/price/inventory sync and real-time APIs. Not MRT-native APIs itself, but directly adjacent: it's the evidence that MuleSoft won't be ready soon, reinforcing why an MRT-native stopgap is needed.
- **[7.1b Third Party Credentials](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/268337165)** — MuleSoft host/token/JWKS credentials are still "Not yet requested," flagged as a hard blocker on technical design.

**Gap:** nothing documents SCAPI/OCAPI shopper endpoints, auth, or payload shape in a way usable for BM/FE work today — that's the actual spike output needed.

## SFCC-123 — Contentful Integration TSD

Much more is already documented here than for SFCC-122 — this spike is more "synthesize and close gaps" than "start from zero":

- **[Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/318472193)** — the most substantial existing doc. Covers environment topology (6-tier, env IDs = MRT push targets), release/alias workflow, API key scopes, **9 locales already mapped to sites.js** (reconciles to your 8 storefronts since EU domestic alone carries en-GB/fr/it/es), content type management split (`scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` for editorial types vs `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` for Studio Experiences), and a setup checklist showing several steps still **incomplete** (MRT env vars per tier, cache-purge webhook, Contentful roles restriction, CI CMA token as GitHub secret).
- **[TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208)** §6 — brief Contentful integration summary (editorial content only, fetched at runtime via CDA) but **Open Item #3: "Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope" — Owner: Frontend Dev, Status: Open**. This is essentially SFCC-123's core task, tracked but unresolved.
- **[04.1.17 Homepage and Content](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/303071234)** (HPC-001–012) — confirmed functional requirements for the Contentful content model: global CMS authoring, preview environment, CMS media library, locale-specific content, Transperfect translation ingestion, global-vs-local content model, page builder templates. Note the open comment on **HPC-001**: *"Open Discussion: Product Names/Prices - SFCC vs Contentful — Review with Tim Lavelle, Jasmijn Tsang"* — an unresolved content-ownership boundary question directly relevant to your "handoff boundary" task.
- **[2.4 Decision Log](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/258408463)** DC002 — "Images in Contentful or SFCC" is still **OPEN/TBC** (leaning: editorial in Contentful, product images in SFCC). Load-bearing for the content model design.
- **[Product Integration Register](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/257163278)** (INT-002) — open questions: how content types are structured for PLP vs PDP, whether Contentful Studio preview scope is included, image CDN strategy (Contentful Images API vs SFCC DIS).
- **[7.1b Third Party Credentials](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/268337165)** — Contentful CDA/CPA tokens, Space ID, env ID, webhook secret all "Not yet requested," flagged **hard blocker**.
- **[Dependencies](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/310050860)** — "T1 Contentful CMS Readiness," Squad A/Sprint 1, also blank owner/status.

**Gap:** the integration *pattern/data flow* (Contentful → MRT → SFCC) and the Accenture-vs-incoming-squad handoff boundary aren't written up anywhere as a single artefact yet — existing docs are fragments (setup mechanics in one page, functional requirements in another, an unresolved decision in a third). That synthesis is what SFCC-123 needs to produce.

---

**Bottom line:** SFCC-122 is closer to a blank slate — there's adjacent evidence (why it's needed) but no MRT API inventory anywhere. SFCC-123 has substantial existing material to draw from (Contentful CMS Setup & Operations doc is a strong technical foundation) but the content model, integration pattern, and handoff boundary are still open items scattered across three separate pages that this spike should consolidate. Want me to draft either deliverable using these sources as a starting point?

Defines the dependency order of the build. Claude reads this to understand what code exists at
each stage. **When working in a sprint, do not reference code, components, hooks, or
integrations from a later sprint — they do not exist yet.**

Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story.

For *what is currently done vs pending* within the active sprint, see
[projectState.md](./projectState.md). This file is the dependency map; `projectState.md`
is the live progress tracker.

---

## Current position

**Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress).**
See [projectState.md](./projectState.md) for the live breakdown.

---

## Sprint 1 — 29 Jun – 10 Jul

**Squad A (FED):**
- Common UI Components
- Homepage & Navigation (Part 1)
- Regional Storefront (Part 1)

**Squad B (FED):**
*Not started yet* 

---

## Sprint 2 — 13 Jul – 24 Jul

**Depends on:** Sprint 1 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Homepage & Navigation (Part 2)
- Regional Storefront (Part 2)
- PDP (Part 1)
- PLP (Part 1)

**Squad B (FED):**
*Not started yet*

---

## Sprint 3 — 27 Jul – 7 Aug

**Depends on:** Sprint 2 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- PDP (Part 2)
- PLP (Part 2)
- Cart

**Squad B (FED):**
- Search & Recommendations

---

## Sprint 4 — 10 Aug – 21 Aug

**Depends on:** Sprint 3 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Checkout Flow & Delivery (excl. custom payments that will be done in Sprint 6)

**Squad B (FED):**
- Promotions

---

## Sprint 5 — 24 Aug – 4 Sep

**Depends on:** Sprint 4 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Order Management

**Squad B (FED):**
- Store Locator
- Zimmerse

---

## Sprint 6 — 7 Sep – 11 Sep

**Depends on:** Sprint 5 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Payments (Adyen, etc)
- Credit Notes & Gift Cards (GiveX)

**Squad B (FED):**
- Zimmerse

---

## Sprint 7

**Depends on:** Sprint 6 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Returns & Refunds

**Squad B (FED):**
- SEO & Analytics (GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, etc)

---

## How Claude uses this file

When implementing a feature, Claude checks which sprint it belongs to and does not reference
components, hooks, or integrations from later sprints.

If a task requires something from a later sprint, Claude stops and asks:
> "This feature depends on [X] which is Sprint [N] work. Should I build a placeholder, or is
> Sprint [N] already complete?"

Reference this file in prompts when sprint context matters:
> "We are currently in Sprint 1. Build the global header skeleton. Do not wire up basket
> state — that is Sprint 3."

3. **HMAC signing secret (or token mechanism).** Provide the per-environment secret/credential Omneo issues for the customer-scoped embed auth. Without it the Omneo ID proxy authentication cannot be exercised end-to-end; until it is provided, the integration can only be developed against a mock.

## 5. GiveX

1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** The integration team to publish the request and response schema for the MuleSoft balance-check endpoint (`POST /givex/balance` placeholder) — the request carries both the card number and the PIN (secure PINs are enabled) — plus the error taxonomy that maps GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, including the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the storefront cannot implement the call against a real MuleSoft instance. **Owner:** MuleSoft — GiveX supplies the underlying failure-code list; Zimmermann owns the final customer-facing message copy.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route. **Owner:** MuleSoft (host / token / thresholds); the MRT-edge WAF / bot / rate-limit config is ours.
3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT balance-check route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request — this is not yet decided. If a CAPTCHA is used, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login (no new provisioning). **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## 6. Booxi

Boutique appointment history is a PWA-direct read (PWA → MRT → Booxi); scope and timeline are TBC.

1. **Storefront scope and timeline (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope, and confirm the target sprint. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments — whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC / Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

## 7. Adyen

1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.

## 8. Global-e

1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply: (a) the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers; and (b) the `postMessage` schema and trusted sender origin for iframe resize and order-completion signals — the PWA listener must verify `event.origin` against this value before acting. Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order, to decide between rendering full order detail or a "View on tracking page" fallback. Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

## 9. Google Maps

1. **Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project and per-environment API keys.** Zimmermann to provision one Places API key per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without the keys the integration cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

## 10. reCAPTCHA

1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only, for MRT token verification) per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK. Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

## 11. Narvar

1. **Per-environment Narvar retailer ID and CONVERT API key.** Provide one set per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these the widget cannot be exercised against a real Narvar account.

2. **Didomi consent category for Narvar Promise.** Confirm which Didomi category the CONVERT widget falls under (Performance?). This determines whether the widget loads for EU and UK users who accept Performance cookies but decline Analytics or Marketing.

## 12. Didomi

1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.

## 13. GTM (with Tell No Lies/Zimm)

1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). Zimmermann/Accenture to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** The data layer is a single shared artifact. Tell No Lies to confirm the storefront's proposed event and attribute schema (page views, product impressions, add-to-cart, begin-checkout, purchase and related ecommerce events, plus consent state and user identifiers) satisfies both GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) and the frontend-direct data-layer consumers (Optimizely, Crazy Egg — not GTM tags). Any additional attributes Optimizely needs for segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg needs for filtering (AAB-005) must be raised at this point.

## 14. Inside Chat

1. **The script tag.** From Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens (the equivalent of what Tryzens hardcoded in Magento).
2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Inside Chat is now a direct PWA head tag (not via GTM — confirmed 2026-07-10). Zimmermann to provide the Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

## 15. Optimizely (with Zimm/TNL)

Optimizely Web is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent.

1. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Optimizely (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 16. Crazy Egg (with Zimm/TNL)

Crazy Egg (heatmaps / session recording) is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm).

1. **Crazy Egg account / site ID per environment.** Zimmermann to provide the account / site ID (script), confirming whether a single account serves all environments or one per tier.
2. **Masking configuration ownership.** Confirm that Tell No Lies owns and applies the session-recording masking configuration (payment and PII fields suppressed) inside the Crazy Egg application. The storefront-side scope is confirmed (AAB-005): the PWA populates the data layer and renders maskable fields with stable selectors; masking itself is outside the PWA.
3. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Crazy Egg (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 17. Measmerize

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## 18. Vimeo

Vimeo is used for product video (PDP) and editorial video (content pages via Contentful CMS). The embed loads client-side as a facade-loaded iframe.

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — suppresses Vimeo's tracking cookies, no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." Zimmermann to confirm before PDP video implementation begins. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

Scope: architecture — stack, customisation model, integrations, regional/multi-site, SSR/SEO, performance, accessibility, testing, CI/CD. 5	---
6	
7	## 1. Purpose & Scope
8	
9	This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at www.zimmermann.com — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.
10	
11	**In scope:**
12	
13	- Stack and build pipeline
14	- The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
15	- Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 8 storefronts in 6 regions
16	- Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
17	- SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
18	- Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
19	- Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
20	- Open decisions requiring client input before build

22	**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design

25	
26	## 2. Solution Overview
27	
28	A single PWA Kit codebase serves 8 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly (via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) for read operations: order history, order details, boutique stock checks (Find in Boutique, Collect in Boutique), GiveX balance check, and real-time stock availability. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.
29	
30	The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.

93	Legend / boundaries:
94	
95	- **PWA → Contentful, Vimeo, Didomi, GTM (via Addingwell), Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, Narvar Promise, Adyen Drop-In:** browser-direct; no SFCC involvement. GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, and Inside Chat load post-Didomi-consent only.

97	- **PWA → SFCC:** all commerce data (catalogue, cart, pricing, customer, orders) via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`.
98	- **SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore / AP21 / Omneo / Narvar:** write and sync flows initiated by SFCC.

123	| ------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |

133	## 4. Customisation Model
134	
135	This project uses the Salesforce PWA Kit's _template extensibility_ model. `@salesforce/retail-react-app` is consumed as an unmodified npm dependency, not a forked copy of the repository.
136	
137	All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.
138	
139	**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.
140	
141	**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) will also live in the `overrides/` folder.
142	
143	### 4.1 Environment Configuration
144	
145	All secrets and per-tier identifiers are injected as **Managed Runtime environment variables**. Unless public identifiers, they must never be committed to source control or exposed in client-side bundles. The canonical list of every variable the storefront expects is maintained in the project's environment-variable template, grouped by integration with inline comments — that template is the single source of truth. The table below shows the groups so each credential's boundary is clear.

The loader uses both: `${GTM_SERVER_URL}/gtm.js?id=${GTM_CONTAINER_ID}`                                                                                                                                               | Browser-direct — both public, safe in bundle. One pair per environment                                                                                                          |

167	**Security policy:**
168	
169	- Real values live only in local, untracked environment files — one shared file (`.env.shared`, tier-independent) plus one per deployment tier (`.env.<tier>` for dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`). Only a template — variable names tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on their own comment line, no secret values — is committed to source control as `.env.sample`. Two guardrails enforce this: a pre-commit hook that blocks commit if `.env.sample` contains a secret-shaped non-empty value, and a Claude Code rule that instructs the AI assistant never to write real secret values into `.env.sample`.
170	- Public identifiers (e.g. the GTM container ID, Didomi notice ID, SFCC SLAS client ID) may carry placeholder values in the committed template.
171	- Secrets (tokens, license keys, HMAC secrets, server-side API keys) appear in the committed template as the variable name only, with an empty value.
172	- Non-personal shared/tier values can be centrally published and pulled via this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per deployment tier under Settings > Environments), stored as GitHub Environment Variables — write access requires repo Admin (`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), read access is repo-collaborator-wide. This is a deliberate, documented exception to using GitHub Secrets (which cannot be read back via API once set) — see `.env.sample`'s header for the full rationale. Genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal` — your own Jira/Confluence token, your own Contentful CMA token) are always excluded from this and never centralized.
173	- MRT variables are managed per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase.

177	## 5. Multi-Site, Multi-Locale Architecture
178	
179	### 5.1 Storefronts
180	
181	**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions**, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods. 11 active locales total. US/EU domestic and international are configured as separate SFCC sites (REG-006).
182

196	### 5.2 Entry routing
197	
198	- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
199	- **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Non-Oceania human visitors are redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; verified search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt; UA ambiguity fails open (false positives have no SEO cost; missing a real crawler does).
200	- **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.
201	
202	### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale
203	
204	Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.
205	
206	### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed
207	
208	- **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
209	- **Tax model:** SFCC native tax tables (AU GST, UK VAT); Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic (EU domestic added 2026-06-19); Global-e handles tax for international checkout paths.
210	- **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
211	- **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.
212	
213	### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts
214	
215	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):
216	
217	- **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
218	- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
219	- **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
220	- **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

235	## 7. Integration Map
236	
237	### 7.1 Classification model
238	
239	Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's documented auth model — a publishable key implies browser-direct is safe; a secret key forces a server-side hop.
240	
241	- **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
242	- **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
243	- **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
244	- **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
245	- **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).
246	
247	A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.
248	
249	> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.

307	## 8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation
308	
309	### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)
310	
311	All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.
312	
313	#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type
314	
315	PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.
316	
317	| Page type                                                         | Pattern                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                            |
318	| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
319	| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages                | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server                                                                                                                                                                | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical                                                                                                                                                                     |
320	| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
321	| Search results, filtered PLP states                               | **SSR shell + CSR data**                                                                                                                                                                                             | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven                                                                                                                                        |
322	
323	The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.
324	
325	### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang
326	
327	Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.
328	
329	### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots
330	
331	Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.
332	
333	### 8.4 Structured data
334	
335	Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:
336	
337	- **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
338	- **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
339	- **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
340	- **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).
341	
342	### 8.5 URL strategy
343	
344	- Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
345	- Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
346	- 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.
347	
348	### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)
349	
350	No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.
351	
352	---
353	
354	## 9. Performance Strategy
355	
356	LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.
357	
358	| Metric                    | Target |
359	| ------------------------- | ------ |
360	| LCP (mobile p75)          | ≤ 2 s  |
361	| Lighthouse Performance    | ≥ 0.80 |
362	| Lighthouse Accessibility  | ≥ 0.90 |
363	| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |
364	
365	### 9.1 Third-party defer rule
366	
367	Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags including the Inside Chat widget, via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.
368	
369	### 9.2 Other levers
370	
371	- **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
372	- **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:
373	  - **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
374	  - **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
375	  - Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
376	- Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
377	- Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.
378	
379	### 9.3 Where performance is measured
380	
381	The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.
382	
383	> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.
384	
385	---
386	
387	## 10. Accessibility
388	
389	**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, with WCAG 2.1 AA as the floor that is always met.
390	
391	**Automated coverage:**
392	
393	- axe-core via `vitest-axe` at the unit layer and `axe-playwright` at the E2E layer
394	- Storybook a11y addon at component level during development
395	- Lighthouse CI accessibility score ≥ 0.90 in the SIT gate
396	
397	**Manual coverage:** delegated to Zimmermann's existing accessibility vendor (unconfirmed — vendor, screen-reader / browser matrix, and audit cadence to be supplied by Zimmermann).
398	
399	---
400	
401	## 11. Consent & Marketing
402	
403	### 11.1 Didomi gating (REG-048–056)
404	
405	- Cookie consent banner on first visit, all storefronts; preferences persist across sessions and are reviewable/updatable per category at any time.
406	- **No third-party tracking or marketing script loads until consent is granted** — including GTM (and the tags Tell No Lies loads downstream: Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, GA4, etc.), the PWA-direct head tags Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg (AAB-004/005), Inside Chat, Narvar widgets.
407	- **reCAPTCHA is not a tracking script** (CRM-008). It loads on register / login form interaction only, deferred to keep it off LCP. **Regional split:** in **EU & UK** it is consent-gated and loads only after Didomi consent — with the accepted consequence that a visitor who declines consent is never challenged, so reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection there. In **all other regions** it loads on form interaction regardless of consent state.
408	- GTM integrated with Didomi for **Google Consent Mode v2**; hashed email passed at order confirmation for Enhanced Conversions.
409	- Where consent state cannot be determined, the system **fails closed** — no third-party scripts load.
410	- Per-storefront consent defaults are specified under REG-054.
411	
412	### 11.2 Marketing opt-in sync
413	
414	`FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys` is the opt-in sync chain (REG-058, REG-059). Sync failures queue and retry silently — they never block the user flow. Trigger points (guest at order placement, registered at registration and My Account preference updates) are functional detail, out of scope for this TSD.
415	
416	### 11.3 GDPR touchpoints in the PWA
417	
418	GDPR fulfilment (DSAR, right-to-erasure, retention, breach reporting per REG-060–067) is handled by the SFCC GDPR cartridge and BM configuration — out of scope for this TSD. PWA-side touchpoints are limited to:
419	
420	- Localised privacy policy pages, served from Contentful per storefront.
421	- The consent UI itself (covered in 11.1).
422	- Surfacing the customer-initiated erasure / data-export entry point in My Account where exposed by SFCC.
423	
424	### 11.4 Didomi consent gate reference
425	
426	Implementation reference for the PWA: which Didomi purpose / vendor ID gates each third-party script. All IDs are **TBC — none have been received from Zimmermann yet.** Guesses are in brackets to orient the conversation.
427	
428	> Didomi purpose IDs for the three declared categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051), plus per-environment Notice IDs, are open items (§12.1 / §12.2 of the Open Items register). All vendor-specific IDs below depend on those being provisioned first.
429	
430	| Integration                                                          | Didomi purpose / vendor ID                                          | Scope                                  | Open item ref |
431	| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
432	| **GTM (Addingwell)** — loads Meta, GA4, Pinterest, TikTok downstream | Handled by Tell No Lies in the GTM container / Addingwell workspace | All storefronts                        | —             |
433	| **Inside Chat**                                                      | TBC                                                                 | All storefronts                        | §14.1         |
434	| **Optimizely Web**                                                   | TBC (Analytics?)                                                    | US storefront only                     | §15.2         |
435	| **Crazy Egg**                                                        | TBC (Analytics?)                                                    | All storefronts                        | §16.3         |
436	| **Narvar Promise**                                                   | TBC (Analytics/Performance? from Narvar/Zimm?)                      | Domestic storefronts only              | §11.2         |
437	| **reCAPTCHA v3**                                                     | n/a — no consent required; loads on form interaction                | All except EU & UK                     | —             |
438	| **reCAPTCHA v3**                                                     | TBC                                                                 | EU & UK storefronts only               | §10.2         |
439	| **Measmerize**                                                       | TBC                                                                 | PDP only                               | §17.1         |
440	| **Vimeo**                                                            | TBC (Marketing/Analytics? use `dnt=1` if no consent)                | PDP + editorial pages, all storefronts | §18.1         |
441	
442	---
443	
444	## 12. Graceful Degradation
445	
446	Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.
447	
448	| System                   | Failure mode                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
449	| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
450	| Contentful               | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
451	| Global-e                 | Surface explicit error; do not silently fall back to SFCC for international checkout                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

# Technical Solution Design — Zimmermann SFCC PWA (Architecture)

_Last updated 2026-07-13 (Security policy section updated for the new `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>` split and GitHub Environments — see `npm run env`). Scope: architecture — stack, customisation model, integrations, regional/multi-site, SSR/SEO, performance, accessibility, testing, CI/CD. Requirement IDs (e.g. DMU-030, REG-041) reference the **Zimmermann Functional Requirements** spreadsheet._

---

## 1. Purpose & Scope

This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at www.zimmermann.com — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.

**In scope:**

- Stack and build pipeline
- The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
- Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 8 storefronts in 6 regions
- Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
- SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
- Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
- Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
- Open decisions requiring client input before build

**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design

---

## 2. Solution Overview

A single PWA Kit codebase serves 8 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly (via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) for read operations: order history, order details, boutique stock checks (Find in Boutique, Collect in Boutique), GiveX balance check, and real-time stock availability. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.

The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.

```
                         ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                         │        Customer browser:        │
                         │ SSR'd HTML + hydrated React PWA │
                         └────────────────┬────────────────┘
                                          │
            ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
            │                             │                                 │
   CDN (Akamai / SFCC default)   Third-party SaaS APIs             (browser handoff
            │                    (browser-direct; no SFCC           at checkout for
            │                     involvement):                     int'l markets)
            │                                                       ─────────────
   PWA Kit (Managed Runtime)       • Contentful                       Global-e
   React 18, SSR + CSR             • Didomi (CMP)                    (international
   overrides/ on                   • Adyen Drop-In (card capture      checkout owner)
   @salesforce/retail-               + tokenisation at checkout)
   react-app v10                   Post-consent:
                                   • GTM via Addingwell (loads:
   MRT-proxied (key server-side):    Meta, GA4, Pinterest,
     • Google Maps Places            TikTok, Inside Chat)
     • GiveX balance check         • Optimizely Web (US only)
       (→ MuleSoft → GiveX)        • Crazy Egg
     • MuleSoft (direct calls)     • Narvar Promise (domestic only)
     • Booxi (boutique appts)      • reCAPTCHA v3 (form interaction;
     • reCAPTCHA token verify        secret verified by MRT)
       (→ Google siteverify)
            │ ▲
            │ │
            │ │
            │ │
            │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │      reads: order history/details,               │
            │             stock check, GiveX balance check     │
            ▼                                                  │
   ┌──────────────────────────────┐         ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
   │   Salesforce Commerce Cloud  │         │             MuleSoft               │
   │   (catalogue, pricebooks,    │─────────│           (middleware)             │
   │    domestic checkout, BM,    │         │                                    │
   │    GDPR cartridge)           │         └────────────────┬───────────────────┘
   │                              │                          │
   └──────────────┬───────────────┘         ┌────────┬───────┼────────┐
                  │                         │        │       │        │
                  │                         NewStore  AP21    Omneo   Narvar
                  ▼                           OMS   (loyalty  (CRM→   (EDD,
   ┌──────────────┬─────────────────────┐           product   Emarsys tracking,
   │ SFCC server-side integrations:     │           master;   email;  returns
   │  • Adyen (domestic payments;       │           product/  iFrame) — dom.)
   │    /payments + 3DS server API)     │           price feed
   │  • GiveX (validate/redeem/refund   │           → SFCC)
   │    via NewStore adapter)           │
   │  • Avalara (tax: US dom, NZ, NC,   │
   │    EU domestic)                    │
   │  • Global-e (server-side; NOT via  │
   │    MuleSoft; separate from the     │
   │    checkout handoff — see legend): │
   │    – FX rates → pricebooks (34..43)│
   │    – catalogue CSV / SFTP (PRC-54) │
   │    – GiveX redeem/refund hooks (44)│
